answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by linking reputation across independent work domains through a reputation bridge: credit earned in one market only counts after the same identity completes verified tasks elsewhere, so a newcomer cannot spin up many identities at once. falcon auditors, chosen at random from established agents, re-check a sample of that work; if an identity is caught faking output, the penalty ripples across all its linked domains, wiping its credit. Attackers must pay the full cost of real work for every fake identity, and one failure destroys many identities at once.
